Reading: the Encyclical of the Eastern P.front: Who is 'the protector of religion', according to the 1848 Encyclical?
Reading: the Encyclical of the Eastern P.back: '**The very body of the Church, even the people themselves**': no patriarch or council can change the faith alone.

Reading: the Encyclical of the Eastern P.front: The four witnesses to the faith named in the 1848 Encyclical
Reading: the Encyclical of the Eastern P.back: The faith that **the Apostles preached**, **the Ecumenical Councils confirmed**, **the teachers handed down**, and **the martyrs' blood ratified**.

The baptism of Rus' (988).back: Grand Prince baptised in **988**; had Kiev baptised in the Dnieper. **Equal-to-the-Apostles**; feast **15 July**.
Princess baptised in Constantinople about **957**; grandmother of Vladimir; **Equal-to-the-Apostles**, 11 July.
One who **accepts an unjust death in Christ's spirit**, though not killed for confessing the faith; first, **Sts Boris and Gleb** (1015).

Kievan Rus' and the Mongol age: the Cave.back: Founded by **Sts Antony (died 1073) and Theodosius (died 1074)**; the mother of Russian monasticism.
Founder of the **Trinity Lavra**; restored coenobitic life; blessed Dmitry Donskoy before **Kulikovo (1380)**; feast **25 September**.

Kievan Rus' and the Mongol age: the Cave.front: Non-possessors and possessors: the debate around 1500
Kievan Rus' and the Mongol age: the Cave.back: **St Nil of Sora**: monks without estates, in hesychast poverty. **St Joseph of Volokolamsk**: lands for worship and charity. **Both glorified.**

Moscow as patriarchate, and the Third Ro.back: **Job** installed as first Patriarch of Moscow by **Jeremias II** of Constantinople; confirmed 1590 and 1593, fifth in the diptychs.
Idea of the monk **Philotheus of Pskov** (1510s–1520s): two Romes had fallen, Moscow is the third, there will be no fourth.
Russian bishops elect **St Jonah** metropolitan without Constantinople, after rejecting the Union of Florence.

Patriarch Nikon and the Old Believers.back: Bringing Russian books and rites into line with the **contemporary Greek**: three-fingered sign of the cross, triple alleluia.
Those who refused Nikon's reforms; divided into **priested**, **priestless** and **Edinoverie** (in communion with Moscow, since 1800).

Patriarch Nikon and the Old Believers.front: What did the Russian Church decide about the old rites in 1971?
Patriarch Nikon and the Old Believers.back: The Local Council **lifted the anathemas of 1656 and 1667**, declaring the old rites **as honourable and saving** as the new.

The Synodal period of the Russian Church.back: Peter the Great's statute, drafted by **Feofan Prokopovich**, replacing the patriarchate with the **Holy Synod** under a lay **Over-Procurator**.

The Synodal period of the Russian Church.front: Two judgements on the Synodal period
The Synodal period of the Russian Church.back: **Structurally unhealthy** (state control, Western school theology: a 'Western captivity') and **spiritually rich** (Optina, Seraphim, Philokalia, missions).
Restored the **Moscow patriarchate**; chose **St Tikhon** by lot on 5 November 1917 (Old Style).

Missions to the east: Alaska, Siberia an.back: Valaam monk of the **1794 Kodiak mission**; hermit of Spruce Island; first saint glorified by the OCA (**1970**).
Priest on Unalaska, translator into Aleut, **Bishop of Kamchatka and the Aleutians (1840)**, **Metropolitan of Moscow (1868)**.
Arrived **1861**; translated the Scriptures and services into Japanese; Tokyo cathedral **1891**; glorified **1970**.

The Serbian Church: from St Sava to the.back: Founded **Hilandar** (1198) with his father; first archbishop of the **autocephalous Serbian Church (1219)**; feast 14 January.
Serbian patriarchate from **1346**; restored **1557**; abolished **1766**. A united Serbian patriarchate was restored in **1920**.
Battle in which **Prince Lazar** fell against the Ottomans; venerated as martyr. Kosovo is the heartland of Serbian Orthodoxy.

The Bulgarian and Romanian churches.back: Organising the Church **by nationality**, with overlapping ethnic churches in one place; condemned by a council in **Constantinople**.
Bulgarian church created by the Sultan's decree; declared schismatic **1872**, schism lifted **1945**; patriarchate restored **1953**.
Autocephaly declared **1865**, recognised by Constantinople **1885**; patriarchate **1925**.

The churches of Greece, Cyprus and Alban.front: Autocephaly of the Church of Greece
The churches of Greece, Cyprus and Alban.back: **Declared 1833** by the Greek state; **recognised by Constantinople's tomos in 1850**.

The churches of Greece, Cyprus and Alban.front: The three privileges of the Archbishop of Cyprus (488)
The churches of Greece, Cyprus and Alban.back: Granted by Emperor Zeno after Barnabas's relics were found: **red ink, imperial sceptre, purple**.
Missionary bishop who **rebuilt the Albanian Church** from 1992 after its destruction in 1967; succeeded by **Joan** (2025).

The smaller churches: Poland, the Czech.back: Czech Orthodox bishop **shot by the Nazis** after his cathedral sheltered Heydrich's assassins; new martyr.
**Autonomous under Constantinople (1923)**; one of Finland's two national churches; keeps **Pascha by the Gregorian calendar**.

The smaller churches: Poland, the Czech.front: Why are there two Orthodox churches in Estonia?
The smaller churches: Poland, the Czech.back: The **Apostolic Orthodox Church** (autonomous under **Constantinople**, revived **1996**) and the **Moscow-linked church**; the 1996 revival caused a months-long Moscow–Constantinople break.

The Church of Georgia.back: **Equal-to-the-Apostles, Enlightener of Georgia**; converted King Mirian III in the **320s or 330s**; cross of vine branches; feast 14 January.
**Abolished by Russia in 1811**; **restored 1917**; recognised by Moscow **1943** and Constantinople **1990**.
Led the Georgian revival from **1977**; died **17 March 2026**; succeeded by **Shio III** (enthroned 12 May 2026).

Antioch in the Arab world.back: The Arabic-speaking Orthodox of Syria and Lebanon, called *Rum* (Romans) for keeping the Byzantine faith.
A disputed election: **Cyril VI** entered communion with Rome (the **Melkite Greek Catholics**); Constantinople appointed **Sylvester** for the Orthodox.
Syrian-born; in **1904** the **first Orthodox bishop consecrated in North America**; glorified 2000.

Alexandria and Jerusalem today.back: **Pope and Patriarch of Alexandria and All Africa**; **Theodore II** since 2004.
The **Greek monastic brotherhood** that governs the Patriarchate of Jerusalem and guards the Orthodox share in the holy places.
Fire brought out of **Christ's tomb by the Patriarch of Jerusalem** on Great and Holy Saturday, received by pilgrims as a miracle.

The Russian Church under Soviet rule (19.front: The 1927 Declaration of Metropolitan Sergius: the two readings
The Russian Church under Soviet rule (19.back: **A necessary compromise** to keep the Church legally alive; or **a betrayal** placing her at a persecuting state's service. Many who refused became martyrs.
Near Moscow: **over 20,000 shot in 1937–1938**, including about a thousand who suffered for their faith; now a place of pilgrimage.
Ended the separation of **ROCOR** and the **Moscow Patriarchate**.

The new martyrs and confessors of the tw.back: One who **suffered for Christ** by prison, torture or exile, **but was not killed**.

The new martyrs and confessors of the tw.front: Synaxis of the New Martyrs and Confessors of Russia
The new martyrs and confessors of the tw.back: Kept on the **Sunday nearest 25 January (Old Style)**; over a thousand glorified by the **Council of 2000**.
**Surgeon and bishop**, repeatedly exiled; kept operating and writing medicine; venerated as a confessor.

Rebirth after communism, and the Ecumeni.back: Treaty of Lausanne: about **1.2 million Orthodox expelled from Turkey** to Greece; Orthodoxy in Asia Minor ended almost entirely.
The Patriarchate's school near Istanbul, **closed 1971**; as of November 2026 restored but its **reopening as a school not settled**.

Rebirth after communism, and the Ecumeni.front: The Ecumenical Patriarch's primacy: the two views
Rebirth after communism, and the Ecumeni.back: **Constantinople**: duties of coordination, appeal and initiative (diaspora, autocephaly). **Moscow**: primacy of honour; pan-Orthodox matters need all churches' consent.

The diaspora: Orthodoxy in Western Europ.back: Russian émigré theological school: **Bulgakov, Florovsky, Afanasiev, Schmemann, Meyendorff**.
Regional gatherings of **all canonical bishops in the diaspora**, chaired by Constantinople's bishop, to prepare a canonical solution.

The diaspora: Orthodoxy in Western Europ.front: Why are overlapping jurisdictions in the diaspora a canonical problem?
The diaspora: Orthodoxy in Western Europ.back: The canons require **one bishop in one city** (Nicaea I, canon 8), and ethnic division recalls **ethnophyletism**. All agree; they differ on the remedy.

The OCA and Orthodoxy in North America.back: Autocephaly granted by **Moscow** to the former Metropolia; recognised as autocephalous by some churches, **not by Constantinople** and most others.
Bishop who built **St Nicholas Cathedral, New York**, founded St Tikhon's Monastery and planned a **multi-ethnic American church**.
Greek Catholic priest who led his parish into Orthodoxy (**1891**), followed by tens of thousands; glorified 1994.

The calendar question: Julian, Revised J.front: Revised Julian calendar: who devised it, and until when it matches the Gregorian
The calendar question: Julian, Revised J.back: Proposed by **Milutin Milanković**, adopted at the **Pan-Orthodox Congress of 1923**; identical to the Gregorian **until 2800**.

The calendar question: Julian, Revised J.front: Why do Orthodox churches differ on Christmas but not on Pascha?
The calendar question: Julian, Revised J.back: **Fixed feasts** follow either the Julian or Revised Julian calendar; **Pascha** is computed by the **Julian Paschalion** everywhere except Finland.

The calendar question: Julian, Revised J.front: Is the calendar a matter of dogma among the canonical churches?
The calendar question: Julian, Revised J.back: **No.** Julian and Revised Julian churches remain **in full communion** and concelebrate.

The Old Calendarists: the case for separ.back: Greek **Old Calendarists**, separated from the Church of Greece after **1924**; bishops from **1935**; several synods today.
Liturgical unity is part of unity of faith; the 1924 change was **uncanonical** and **linked to ecumenism**; separating from error is a patristic duty (canon 15 of 861).

The Old Calendarists: the case for separ.front: The canonical churches' strongest case against separation
The Old Calendarists: the case for separ.back: The calendar is **not dogma**; **schism is the graver sin**; canon 15 concerns condemned heresy; the Julian-calendar churches **stayed in communion**.

Autocephaly: how a church becomes self-h.back: The **official decree** by which a church is granted autocephaly or autonomy.
The bishops of each nation recognise **the first among them as head**, and he does nothing without them: the principle of the local church.

Autocephaly: how a church becomes self-h.front: Who grants autocephaly? Constantinople's and Moscow's answers
Autocephaly: how a church becomes self-h.back: **Constantinople**: the First See, by tomos, with recognition after. **Moscow**: the **mother church**, with the **consent of all**. Unresolved, so left off the 2016 agenda.

Looking back: one Church in many lands.front: Five sentences that sum up the Church's history since 1453
Looking back: one Church in many lands.back: A **communion of local churches**; mostly **without a friendly state**; each nation **in its own language** but **never divided by ethnicity**; the 20th century **an age of martyrs**; today's disputes are **about order, not faith**.

Looking back: one Church in many lands.front: Three questions Orthodox Christians answer differently (Stage 11)
Looking back: one Church in many lands.back: **The calendar**, **the Old Calendarist separation**, and **who grants autocephaly**.

Context: Orthodox theology meets the mod.front: What did modern Orthodox theology set out to recover?
Context: Orthodox theology meets the mod.back: A theology in the Church's **own idiom**, the Fathers, the Liturgy and prayer, after centuries of **borrowed Western textbook forms**.
The **academic** recovery of the Fathers (Florovsky, Lossky, Stăniloae) and the **spiritual** witness of elders and saints (Silouan, Paisios, Porphyrios).

Khomiakov, the Slavophiles and sobornost.back: Russian lay theologian and leader of the **Slavophiles**; taught the Church as a **free organism of grace and love**.
From *sobornyi*, Slavonic for 'catholic' in the Creed: the **conciliar, communal wholeness** of the Church, in which truth is held by all together.

Khomiakov, the Slavophiles and sobornost.front: How do Orthodox writers judge Khomiakov?
Khomiakov, the Slavophiles and sobornost.back: **Admirers**: the first to think from inside the Church's life, forerunner of the return to the Fathers. **Critics**: defined the Church too much by contrast with the West, with Romantic borrowings.

Reading: Khomiakov on the Church as one.back: Short numbered essay on the Church, printed after his death; English by **W. J. Birkbeck (1895)**.

Reading: Khomiakov on the Church as one.front: Khomiakov: why is the Church one?
Reading: Khomiakov on the Church as one.back: 'Her unity follows of necessity **from the unity of God**': a unity of grace living in many persons, like **members of a living body**.

Reading: Khomiakov on the Church as one.front: Khomiakov: 'he falls alone; but no one is saved alone'
Reading: Khomiakov on the Church as one.back: Sin isolates; **salvation is communion**: whoever believes, loves or prays is already in the Church's communion of faith, love and prayer.

The Russian religious renaissance and Fr.back: Marxist economist turned priest; first dean of **St Sergius, Paris**; author of a trilogy on Godmanhood; teacher of **sophiology**.
Bulgakov's teaching that **Divine Wisdom (Sophia)** is the bond between God and creation; condemned locally in **1935**, never judged pan-Orthodoxly.
Priest, mathematician and theologian of the Russian renaissance; **shot in the Soviet camps**.

Florovsky and the neo-patristic synthesi.back: Patristic scholar of Paris, St Vladimir's, Harvard and Princeton; called for the **neo-patristic synthesis** (Athens, **1936**).
Florovsky's programme: **acquire the mind of the Fathers** and answer new questions in their spirit, not merely quote them.
Orthodox content in **Latin and Protestant forms**: his diagnosis of Russian theology since the 17th century (*Ways of Russian Theology*, 1937).

Vladimir Lossky and the mystical theolog.back: Lay theologian in Paris; *The Mystical Theology of the Eastern Church* (**1944**), the most influential modern synthesis of Orthodox doctrine.

Vladimir Lossky and the mystical theolog.front: Lossky: how are theology and mysticism related?
Vladimir Lossky and the mystical theolog.back: **They are one**: no Christian mysticism without theology, no theology without mysticism; doctrine expresses the Church's experience of God.
'**Negative**' theology: knowing God by what He is not; for Lossky the **fundamental attitude** of Orthodox theology, not a stage.

Schmemann, Afanasiev and liturgical theo.back: Dean of **St Vladimir's** (1962–1983); *For the Life of the World* (1963); founder of **liturgical theology** in its modern form.
**Where the Eucharist is celebrated round the bishop, there is the whole Church.** Fr Nicholas Afanasiev (1893–1966).

Schmemann, Afanasiev and liturgical theo.front: lex orandi, lex credendi in Schmemann's liturgical theology
Schmemann, Afanasiev and liturgical theo.back: 'The **rule of prayer** is the **rule of belief**': the Liturgy is not only a source of theology but theology itself.

Meyendorff and the recovery of St Gregor.back: Historian and theologian; *A Study of Gregory Palamas* (**1959**); *Byzantine Theology* (1974); dean of St Vladimir's 1984–1992.

Meyendorff and the recovery of St Gregor.front: What did Meyendorff show about Palamas?
Meyendorff and the recovery of St Gregor.back: That he was **a faithful heir of the Greek Fathers**, not an innovator, and that hesychasm is a theology of the **whole person** transfigured by grace.

St Dumitru Stăniloae.back: Romanian priest-theologian; **Romanian Philokalia** (12 vols); *Orthodox Dogmatic Theology* (1978); imprisoned **1958–1963**; glorified 2024; feast **4 October**.
Creation is **God's gift**, given to be offered back to Him: a **dialogue of love** between God and humanity.

John Zizioulas: being as communion.back: Greek theologian; *Being as Communion* (**1985**); co-chair of the Catholic–Orthodox dialogue.
**Being is communion**: the ultimate reality is persons in relation, the Trinity with the **Father as source**; the **Eucharist makes the Church**.
That the Cappadocians did not mean **'person' in the modern sense**, and that he reads **modern personalist philosophy** into the Fathers. Defenders: he draws out what they taught.

Yannaras, Romanides and the Greek theolo.back: *The Ancestral Sin* (**1957**): the Greek Fathers teach inherited **mortality and corruption**, not inherited guilt; theology as **therapy**.
Greek philosopher-theologian; *Person and Eros* (1976): God and humanity as **persons whose being is relation**.
Greek lay theologian, author of *Deification in Christ*.

St Justin Popović.back: Serbian archimandrite, dogmatician, author of 12 volumes of *Lives of the Saints*; at **Ćelije** monastery from 1948; glorified **2010**.
Christ as **God-Man**, the measure of all things: St Justin's central theme, against **humanism** that puts man in God's place.

St Justin Popović.front: St Justin Popović's view of ecumenism
St Justin Popović.back: The Orthodox Church **is** the One Church; ecumenism that treats churches as **equal parts** denies this: he called it a **pan-heresy**.

Fr Seraphim Rose.back: American convert; hieromonk of **Platina**, California; St Herman Brotherhood (1963); author of *The Soul After Death*. ROCOR blessed preparing his glorification in **May 2026**.
Aerial stations where, in many lives of saints, **demons accuse the soul after death**; a question Orthodox writers answer differently.

Fr Seraphim Rose.front: What is common ground on the toll-houses?
Fr Seraphim Rose.back: The Church teaches a **particular judgement** after death and **prays for the departed**; how the encounter is pictured is **not defined by any council**.

St Silouan the Athonite.back: Russian peasant, monk of **St Panteleimon** on Athos for 46 years; glorified by Constantinople **1987**; feast **24 September**.

St Silouan the Athonite.front: The word St Silouan received in prayer (paraphrase)
St Silouan the Athonite.back: **Keep your mind in hell, and do not despair**: humility and hope together.

St Silouan the Athonite.front: St Silouan: the sign of grace
St Silouan the Athonite.back: **Love for enemies**: one who does not love his enemies does not yet know God.

St Sophrony of Essex.back: Painter, Athonite monk, disciple and biographer of St Silouan; founded **Tolleshunt Knights, Essex (1959)**; glorified **2019**; feast 11 July.

St Sophrony of Essex.front: Monastery of St John the Baptist, Tolleshunt Knights
St Sophrony of Essex.back: Stavropegic monastery of the **Ecumenical Patriarchate** in Essex; monks and nuns; the Jesus Prayer said aloud in common.

St Paisios the Athonite.back: Born at **Farasa, Cappadocia**; Athonite elder at **Panagouda**; buried at **Souroti**; glorified **2015**; feast **12 July**.
St Paisios's counsel: **interpret everything and everyone in the best light**.

St Paisios the Athonite.front: How should the 'prophecies' attributed to St Paisios be treated?
St Paisios the Athonite.back: With caution: **authenticity varies**; read his authenticated *Spiritual Counsels* and set aside sensational collections.

St Porphyrios of Kafsokalyvia.back: Athonite elder from Euboea; **chaplain of the Athens Polyclinic 1940–1973**; glorified **2013**; feast **2 December**.

St Porphyrios of Kafsokalyvia.front: St Porphyrios: how to fight evil
St Porphyrios of Kafsokalyvia.back: **Do not fight it head on**; turn to Christ with love, and the darkness withdraws as light enters a room.

The Orthodox in the ecumenical movement.back: 'Unto the Churches of Christ Everywhere': proposed a **fellowship of churches** for cooperation; a founding text of the ecumenical movement.
By **Patriarch Athenagoras** and **Pope Paul VI**, on **7 December 1965**.

The Orthodox in the ecumenical movement.front: The Orthodox cases for and against ecumenical participation
The Orthodox in the ecumenical movement.back: **For**: witness, charity, the Spirit beyond canonical bounds, Christ's prayer for unity. **Against**: it implies a divided Church, breeds relativism, breaks canons on joint prayer.

The dialogue with the Oriental Orthodox.back: **Coptic, Ethiopian, Eritrean, Syriac, Armenian and Malankara**: the churches that did not receive **Chalcedon (451)**.
Of the Orthodox–Oriental Orthodox Joint Commission (**Anba Bishoy**, 1989; **Chambésy**, 1990): **the same faith in Christ** in different terms.

The dialogue with the Oriental Orthodox.front: Why has communion with the Oriental Orthodox not been restored?
The dialogue with the Oriental Orthodox.back: Questions of **the later ecumenical councils**, of **saints each side condemned** (Leo; Dioscorus, Severus), and **incomplete reception** of the statements.

The Holy and Great Council of 2016.back: Met at **Kolymbari**, Crete; **ten** churches present; **Antioch, Russia, Bulgaria and Georgia** absent; six documents adopted.

The Holy and Great Council of 2016.front: The two views of the 2016 Council's authority
The Holy and Great Council of 2016.back: **Constantinople**: convened by all primates, binding. **The absent churches**: consensus of all was required; a council of the participants only.

Ukraine: the road to the 2018–19 break.front: The two readings of the 1686 documents on Kiev
Ukraine: the road to the 2018–19 break.back: **Constantinople**: a temporary permission by economy for Moscow to ordain the metropolitan. **Moscow**: a full canonical transfer, accepted for three centuries.
Formed at the **Unification Council (15 December 2018)**; **Metropolitan Epiphanius**; tomos signed **5 January 2019**.
The Russian Holy Synod broke communion after Constantinople's decisions of **11 October 2018** on Ukraine.

Ukraine as of November 2026: the churche.front: The UOC council at Feofania (27 May 2022)
Ukraine as of November 2026: the churche.back: Condemned the war, removed Moscow from its statute and declared **full self-sufficiency and independence**, without declaring autocephaly.
Bans organisations **affiliated with the Russian Orthodox Church**; basis of the suit to **dissolve the UOC's Kyiv Metropolis** (pending as of November 2026).

Ukraine as of November 2026: the churche.front: What is common ground among all parties in Ukraine?
Ukraine as of November 2026: the churche.back: **The same faith and sacraments**; the division concerns **jurisdiction, canonical order and church, nation and state** in wartime.

Orthodoxy in Africa.back: Ugandan founder of an African Orthodox movement (**1929**), received by **Alexandria in 1946**; later bishop.
Created by **Moscow** after Alexandria recognised the OCU; rejected by Alexandria as an **uncanonical invasion**.

Social teaching: the Church and the mode.back: Russian Orthodox social teaching: church and state, nation, bioethics, family, war.

Social teaching: the Church and the mode.front: For the Life of the World: Toward a Social Ethos (2020)
Social teaching: the Church and the mode.back: Social document **blessed for publication by the Ecumenical Patriarchate**: the person, pluralism, poverty, peace, creation.

Social teaching: the Church and the mode.front: Day of prayer for creation (1 September)
Social teaching: the Church and the mode.back: Proclaimed by **Patriarch Demetrios** in **1989**, at the start of the Church year.

Other unfolding questions, as of Novembe.back: Received into communion by **Constantinople (May 2022)** without autocephaly; granted **autocephaly by Serbia (June 2022)**; partly recognised.

Other unfolding questions, as of Novembe.front: Why has no Orthodox church changed the date of Pascha?
Other unfolding questions, as of Novembe.back: Many hold that any change needs **pan-Orthodox consensus** and must keep the **Nicene principles**; as of November 2026 none has changed its Paschalion.

Looking back: the Church today, and the.front: Settled and open questions in Orthodoxy
Looking back: the Church today, and the.back: **Settled**: what the councils defined (Trinity, Christ, icons, essence and energies). **Open**: toll-houses, calendar, autocephaly procedure, 2016's authority, ecumenism's terms.

Looking back: the Church today, and the.front: Three last words from the saints of Stage 12
Looking back: the Church today, and the.back: **Khomiakov**: no one is saved alone. **Silouan**: love for enemies is the sign of grace. **Porphyrios**: Christ is joy.
